knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Out= parameter aliasing input storage produces incorrect results
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operators with out= parameters may assume output storage is distinct from input storage; when output aliases or overlaps an input, reads and writes can interfere and hidden backend assumptions may be violated, causing incorrect results.

risk_dimensions.shape: Explore shapes where the output shape can match or overlap an input shape, including square matrices, degenerate dimensions, and view-compatible shapes.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Vary floating-point and integer dtypes; aliasing handling and kernel behavior may differ by dtype.
risk_dimensions.memory: Use out= tensors that alias input storage through the same tensor object, views, slices, or partial overlaps.
risk_dimensions.device: Test CPU and accelerator backends; backend implementations may have different aliasing checks or memory copy behavior.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Exercise eager execution and graph/compiled execution paths, as aliasing behavior may differ.

failure_mechanism.description: The API accepts an out= parameter but may not reject or correctly handle output storage that aliases input storage, leading to overlapping reads and writes that corrupt the result.

input_exploration: Explore out= tensors that are the same object as an input tensor.
Explore out= tensors that are views or slices sharing storage with an input tensor.
Explore partially overlapping and fully overlapping output/input memory arrangements.
Vary shapes so the output shape matches or is compatible with an input view shape.
constraint_awareness: Check API documentation and backend requirements for aliasing or overlap constraints on out= parameters.
Be aware that shape compatibility may determine whether output can alias an input in practice.
Hidden backend assumptions about input/output storage independence may not be validated.
oracle_strategy: Compare the aliased out= result against a reference result computed with a fresh, non-aliased output tensor.
Monitor for crashes, sanitizer reports, or unexpected mutation of input tensors.
Flag any numerical mismatch or memory corruption as a potential bug.

transferability.reason: Any API that exposes an out= parameter or in-place/out-of-place variants may rely on independent output storage; the principle of aliasing or overlapping input/output memory is broadly applicable and not limited to a single operation.

important_considerations: Systematically alias out= with input tensors, including full aliasing and overlapping views.
Use a fresh output reference to detect silent incorrect results.
Vary shape, dtype, device, and execution state to expose backend-specific aliasing assumptions.
generation_strategy: Apply the pattern to any API with an out= parameter or in-place/out-of-place behavior rather than hardcoding a specific operation.
Construct output tensors that intentionally share storage with inputs using the same tensor, views, slices, or expanded views when shape-compatible.
Use a fresh-output reference oracle to detect mismatches and include sanitizers to catch memory corruption.
